mechanism: Estimate a global query foreground pixel prior from foreground/background score densities learned on the reference. Replace a fixed-prior decision with the fitted mixture posterior. This is a conditional prior-shift model, not a calibrated semantic-success probability or an object-count estimator.
difference_from_preceding_candidates: Uses reference background as well as foreground to construct a scalar density model, and unlabeled query likelihood to fit class prevalence. It does not compare object geometry/covariance, seek recurring query components, modify the feature graph or use RGB paths.
inputs: existing MEAN field64 for shared control and exact abstention fallback only
data_exposure: Reference mask supplies foreground/background samples. No query GT, class/fold input, extra image, encoder or external training set is used. Reference centroids and density calibration reuse the same reference samples; this is resubstitution, not independent calibration.
steps: Require at least8 pure foreground samples (coverage>=0.9) and8 pure background samples (coverage<=0.1). Compute coverage-weighted unit centroids; missing samples or degenerate centroids abstain to the original base.
Use the same reference-derived direction for all samples: score(x)=cos(x,mu_F)-cos(x,mu_B), clipped to[-2,2] for rounding. Compute reference and query scalar scores without labels from the query.

Use64 fixed bins on[-2,2]. Normalize class-weighted reference histograms, apply a Gaussian kernel of bandwidth0.1 with each source column normalized, then add1% uniform probability mass and normalize. Interpolate the positive piecewise-linear densities at every query score; endpoint half-bins have constant density.

Fit pi in[1/N,1-1/N] by maximizing mean log(pi*f(s_i)+(1-pi)*b(s_i)). Derivative is mean((f-b)/(pi*f+(1-pi)*b)); second derivative is nonpositive. Endpoint derivative signs give a boundary optimum; otherwise use at most64 bisections with prior bracket tolerance1e-10.

When all query likelihoods have f=b within relative tolerance1e-12, pi is unidentifiable and the primary preserves the original base. Otherwise output the posterior pi*f/(pi*f+(1-pi)*b), with no base blending.

Bilinear upsample the complete posterior field to1024 and threshold>0.5. Save identical-readout controls: balanced pi=0.5, reference foreground coverage mean as pi, and direct signed-centroid score mapped by0.5+0.25*score. Controls and prior values do not count as additional methods.

Use the common prepared CPU backend. Shared MEAN is computed for fair comparison/fallback, but an active candidate depends only on q/r/reference coverage. Seal all predictions before separate query-GT scoring.

prediction.conditional: When the reference foreground/background score densities transfer and query prevalence differs, fitting the prior can improve a threshold over reference prevalence or an arbitrary balanced prior. Identical scores for a true object and a distractor remain indistinguishable.
exact_properties: For fixed positive query f/b, the prior likelihood is concave and strictly concave when any f differs from b; the bisection/endpoint test solves this one-dimensional objective
Token posterior exceeds0.5 iff f(s)/b(s)>(1-pi)/pi; this token inequality does not directly describe the final bilinear1024 mask
Common orthogonal feature transformations preserve centroids, scalar scores and predictions in exact arithmetic
An active candidate has the same prior/posterior regardless of the supplied base field; abstention depends on that fallback

checks.optimization: prior_shift_check.json:32 positive-density cases agree with independent scalar minimization within1.14e-8. Exact expected counts from a three-category mixture recover pi=0.3. Both boundary optima and flat-likelihood abstention checked.
checks.complete_positive: Default full4096x1024 synthetic scene retains all256 designated target tokens and rejects800 distractor tokens. Balanced-prior and direct-margin controls retain both; reference-prior control retains neither. Fitted pi=0.08784 versus true synthetic target fraction0.0625, so correct thresholding here is not proof of calibrated prevalence. The target uses a subset of reference foreground appearances, so this example also is not proof of pure prior-shift transfer.
checks.complete_negative: With unchanged method and a smaller64-token target, fitted pi is0.00430 and the complete token output is empty. This observed failure is retained, without changing bandwidth or prior bounds.
checks.batch: runner_check.json checks active fitting through two-worker inference, unread query-GT sentinels, packed1024 controls and sealed masks. A different supplied source score gives the same fitted candidate prior; shared MEAN is a control/fallback.

counterexamples: Sparse true targets can be discarded when a low fitted prior and overlapping class densities suppress all posterior values below0.5; the64-token example demonstrates this.
Query backgrounds or foreground appearances can differ from the reference. A high likelihood within the supplied mixture does not validate transfer or semantic labels.
The same signed centroid score may describe both a true object and background; no prior separates such pixels.
Multimodal or cancelling foreground/background centroids can lose useful feature information, and some references have no pure background samples.
Histograms, fixed bandwidth, uniform mass and finite reference samples can distort density tails that decide small targets.
Reference resubstitution and spatially correlated tokens make likelihood curvature unsuitable as an independent semantic confidence interval.
A single global prevalence cannot accommodate different local background distributions or occluded parts.

cpu_cost.bound: O(ND+B^2+N*maximum_bisections), B=64; feature normalization/projection plus fixed histograms and scalar fits. Storage O(ND+N+B^2). No encoder, region search or iterative feature-graph solve for the active candidate.
cpu_cost.synthetic_benchmark: prior_shift_check.json records synthetic inputs already loaded; excludes shared MEAN construction, feature I/O,1024 readout and actual cohort scoring.

next_actual_evidence: Compare complete outputs to same-input MEAN and all three simple controls, reporting actual class-summed I/U, photo-group paired intervals, four edit types and timings. Include sparse targets rather than conditioning away the observed failure. User shut down the instance; no actual cohort launched.
novelty: Unverified; mixture proportion estimation, prior shift and density calibration are established ideas
